description:
If you’re an advanced freediver who wants to learn how to fine-tune your lifestyle and training so that you can approach elite freediving levels, then the Master Freediver course is for you. Through focused sessions, you’ll bring your static apnea, dynamic apnea, free immersion, and constant weight skills to the next level. This course will also be a stepping stone for those looking to get into the competitive world of freediving.

The PADI Master Freediver course continues knowledge and skill development with further development in static apnea over 3 minutes and 30 seconds, dynamic apnea to 70 meters/230 feet, free immersion, and constant weight freediving to a minimum of 32 meters/105 feet.

highlights:
**Course Schedule**

*The PADI Master Freediver course consists of three main phases:*

- Classroom/Knowledge development about nutrition, relaxation, and advanced breathing techniques. You’ll study independently using the Freediver online materials as well as an Instructor-led class session. You’ll also complete independent research as part of the Master Freediving Assignment.

- Pool/Confined water session to improve static and dynamic apnea attempts, including a no-fins dynamic apnea.

- Goal – static apnea of 3 minutes, 30 seconds, and dynamic apnea of 70m/230ft.

- Open water sessions to practice mouth-fill equalization, perform warm-up and workup dives for free immersion and constant weight freediving.

- Goal – constant weight Freedive of 32 m/105ft, max 40m/130ft.
highlight_description: The PADI Level Three Master Freediver course is designed for freedivers who are looking to maximize their depths, dive times, and overall knowledge of the sport.
what_to_bring:
- Towel, Swimsuit, swim shorts, sunscreen, water or favorite hydration drinks, and snacks.

- Pool Training Wetsuit - a 3 or 4/3 mm surf suit/triathlon swimsuit or similar is recommended for pool training. Please let us know if you cannot provide your own pool wetsuit.

- Wetsuit - 5mm 2-piece Freediving wetsuit or a 7mm during the winter season.

- Weight Belt with 6 to 14lb of weights, a rubber weight belt with “Marseille buckle” style is highly recommended. By now, you should know how much weight you will need with your wetsuit in saltwater.

- Mask – A small-volume silicone freediving mask in addition to freediving googles, mask defog.

- Noseclip (to use with freediving googles for equalization)

- Safety Lanyard 

- Snorkel - the simpler the better, no dry-snorkel from Scuba.
 
- Fins – Long-blade Freediving fins, fiberglass or carbon fins preferred to really get the most out of your freediving training, but not required.

- Gloves – 3 or 5mm are recommended, depending on the time of the year and your tolerance to cold.

- Equipment bag or gear crate – Something to carry all your freediving gear from the car to the dive site.
special_requirements:
**Prerequisites**

- Provide your own freediving-specific gear
- Be at least 18 years of age 
- Advanced Freediver certification – or qualifying certification from other freediving training agencies – cross-over evaluation will be performed and will not be included in the course fee.
- Have an Emergency First Responder (EFR) certificate or equivalent, not older than 2 years.
- You need adequate swimming skills.
- You need to be in good physical health. 
- Paperwork: Complete the PADI Medical Questionnaire, Freediver Liability Release, and the Statement of Understanding.
faqs:
**What is the PADI Master Freediver Course with Dive California?**

The PADI Master Freediver course is the third level of freediving and includes an instructor-led classroom session, 2 confined water (or pool), and 4 Open Water sessions in the ocean.

The PADI Master Freediver course also includes an e-certification that will allow you to freedive with a buddy in a pool or in the ocean.

**What is included in the PADI Master Freediver course with Dive California?**

- PADI Master Freediver e-Learning study materials
- PADI e-certification
- Instructor-led classroom session
- 2 Confined Water/pool session
- 4 Open Water sessions

**How long does the PADI Master Freediver Course take?**

Our PADI Master Freediver course will take a minimum of 4 days, allowing you to take the course at a relaxed pace.

**What is the minimum age for the PADI Master Freediver Course with Dive California?**

Minimum age for the PADI Freediver course is 18 years of age, in good health, and have adequate swimming skills.

**What should I bring?**

- Towel, Swimsuit, swim shorts, sunscreen, water or favorite hydration drinks, and snacks.

- Pool Training Wetsuit - a 3 or 4/3 mm surf suit/triathlon swimsuit or similar is recommended for pool training. Please let us know if you cannot provide your own pool wetsuit.

- Wetsuit - 5mm 2-piece Freediving wetsuit or a 7mm during the winter season.

- Weight Belt with 6 to 14lb of weights, a rubber weight belt with “Marseille buckle” style is highly recommended. By now, you should know how much weight you will need with your wetsuit in saltwater.

- Mask – A small-volume silicone freediving mask in addition to freediving googles, mask defog.

- Noseclip (to use with freediving googles for equalization)

- Safety Lanyard 

- Snorkel - the simpler the better, no dry-snorkel from Scuba.
 
- Fins – Long-blade Freediving fins, fiberglass or carbon fins preferred to really get the most out of your freediving training, but not required.

- Gloves – 3 or 5mm are recommended, depending on the time of the year and your tolerance to cold.

- Equipment bag or gear crate – Something to carry all your freediving gear from the car to the dive site. 

**Will I receive a certification?**

You will earn a certification recognition after successfully completing this program.
